title: Classical bassists and Koussevitzky's praise
summary: He met no classical bassists in England or during the Tatum years, but Koussevitzky, whom he met briefly in Boston, thought him among the best in jazz around 1938.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you talk to -- meet many classical bassists when you were on that -- when you went to England? Did you meet any?
I don't think I met any.
Now, had you encountered when you were

in America -- I know recently, because I don't want to jump ahead, but recently you've done a lot of work with classical players. But did you meet any, like, say, for instance, in the '40s -- because it was said oftentimes people like Horovitz and others would come and hear, Tatum.
Yeah.
Did you meet any of those people while you were working with Tatum?
Well, I met some of the people who came to visit while I was working with Tatum, but I never did meet any classical bassists.
Well, mention has been made of the fact that Koussevitsky....
Koussevitsky.
Did you meet him?
I met him shortly -- for a short moment when I went to Boston.
Oh, when you --
In earlier years.
Oh, when you were going to school?
Yeah.
Now -- I read somewhere that he was very impressed with your work later on when you started working with the bow.
Yes. He did say that he was, like you
say, he was very impressed with my playing and he could -- he considered me one of the best in the jazz field, you know.
Do you remember when he said this? About what time -- when in your career this was?
Oh, that was -- I think that was somewhere around 1938.
Oh, so he had begun noticing you --
Yeah, oh yes.
-- begun to notice you that soon after you left Boston.
Yes, yes, right.
